summary: For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our team developed MISSION FORGE, an interactive aerospace simulation game and systems architecture tool that bridges the gap between complex orbital mechanics and engaging gameplay. The challenge addresses how to effectively communicate the intricacies of spacecraft engineering, launch logistics, and long-term Earth and space science campaigns to the public and aspiring engineers. MISSION FORGE solves this by putting players in the role of a chief mission architect where they must balance rigorous engineering trade-offs—including mass budgets, power generation, data downlink bandwidth, and financial constraints. By simulating real-world orbital dynamics, scientific data accumulation, and mid-mission crisis management (such as solar flares and telemetry anomalies), our project transforms raw aerospace principles into an accessible, educational experience. It empowers users to explore space exploration design firsthand, fostering deeper STEM interest and spatial systems thinking.
details:
What it does & How it works:

  • Briefing & Setup Lobby: Enables solo or team players to select mission objectives (such as Climate Watch, Deep Space, or Moon Mapper), configure target orbits, and adjust difficulty parameters before starting.
  • Hangar Workbench: An intuitive systems-design hub where players manage four core mission pillars—Planner, Engineer, Science, and Comms—while monitoring real-time telemetry updates.
  • Simulation & Launch Engine: Features a cinematic launch sequence that transitions smoothly into a live, month-by-month telemetry loop, complete with orbital radar tracking and science data downlinks.
  • Crisis Management System: Introduces randomized mid-mission emergencies (like solar flares or gyro glitches) that force players to make high-stakes strategic choices under pressure.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact: Mission Forge transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an accessible, highly engaging experience. It acts as an educational sandbox that teaches players about satellite constraints, power management, and the nuanced decision-making behind real NASA missions.

Tech Stack & Tools: Built using modern HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and custom canvas-based UI animations to deliver high-performance, cross-platform execution directly in the browser with zero backend dependencies.

Creativity & Design Choices: Unlike traditional, static dashboards, Mission Forge combines rigorous engineering physics with fast-paced, gamified decision loops. It features an authentic, dark-themed command-center aesthetic, live black-box flight recorders, and an immersive scoring system that makes systems thinking genuinely fun.
